column3: With `isolation.level` set to `read_committed`, `consumer.poll()` only returns transactional messages which have been committed (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: If set to read_committed, consumer.poll() will only return transactional messages which have been committed.

column3: With `read_uncommitted`, which is the default, `consumer.poll()` returns all messages, even transactional messages which have been aborted (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: If set to read_uncommitted (the default), consumer.poll() will return all messages, even transactional messages which have been aborted.

column3: In `read_committed` mode, `consumer.poll()` only returns messages up to the last stable offset, which is one less than the offset of the first open transaction (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: in read_committed mode, consumer.poll() will only return messages up to the last stable offset (LSO), which is the one less than the offset of the first open transaction.

column3: Messages after messages belonging to ongoing transactions are withheld until the relevant transaction has been completed (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: any messages appearing after messages belonging to ongoing transactions will be withheld until the relevant transaction has been completed.

column3: Messages are always returned in offset order (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: Messages will always be returned in offset order.

column3: In `read_committed` mode, consumers cannot read up to the high watermark when there are in-flight transactions (`kafka-consumer-configs#isolation.level`).
column5: read_committed consumers will not be able to read up to the high watermark when there are in flight transactions.

column3: To enable exactly-once semantics in Kafka Streams, set `processing.guarantee`, whose default value is `at_least_once`, to `StreamsConfig.EXACTLY_ONCE_V2` (`kafka-streams-core-concepts#processing-guarantees`).

column3: In Spring for Apache Kafka, using transactions enables exactly-once semantics, and for a read, process, write sequence the sequence is completed exactly once while the read and process have at-least-once semantics (`spring-kafka-exactly-once#page-title`).
column5: This means that, for a read → process → write sequence, it is guaranteed that the sequence is completed exactly once. (The read and process have at least once semantics).

column3: In RabbitMQ, messages can be redelivered after a network or node failure, and consumers must be prepared to handle deliveries they have seen in the past (`rabbitmq-reliability#consumer-side`).
column5: In the event of network failure (or a node failure), messages can be redelivered, and consumers must be prepared to handle deliveries they have seen in the past.

column3: RabbitMQ recommends that a consumer is designed to be idempotent rather than to explicitly perform deduplication (`rabbitmq-reliability#consumer-side`).
column5: It is recommended that consumer implementation is designed to be idempotent rather than to explicitly perform deduplication.

column3: If the redelivered flag is not set on a RabbitMQ message, it is guaranteed that the message has not been seen before (`rabbitmq-reliability#consumer-side`).
column5: If the redelivered flag is not set then it is guaranteed that the message has not been seen before.

column3: In RabbitMQ, a transactional channel cannot be put into confirm mode, and a channel in confirm mode cannot be made transactional (`rabbitmq-confirms#publisher-confirms`).
column5: A transactional channel cannot be put into confirm mode and once a channel is in confirm mode, it cannot be made transactional.
